name: Low-Level System Design: LRU Cache, Elevator & Ticket Booking
tagline: Translating requirements into clean class hierarchies, explicit state machines, and concurrency-safe interfaces inside a service.
purpose: Build a progressive mental model of Low-Level Design (LLD)—separating entities, value objects, and domain services while guarding concurrent state transitions.

spark.summary: Low-Level Design (LLD) translates high-level requirements into clean class hierarchies, explicit state machines, concurrency-safe interfaces, and extensible design patterns inside a single service or library.
spark.keyTakeaway: When a single bottleneck threatens end-to-end availability, elevator & Ticket Booking, great LLD isolates volatile business rules behind narrow interfaces and explicit state transitions so adding a new pricing rule, eviction policy, or booking workflow never breaks existing code.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** While High-Level Design (HLD) governs distributed services over networks, **Low-Level Design (LLD)** governs the internal architecture of a service or library: **entities** (identity + lifecycle), **value objects** (immutable.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Ticket Seat Hold Lifecycle (Replacing Boolean Flag Soup) (AVAILABLE -> HELD (TTL) -> BOOKED); Guarding Check-Then-Act in Concurrent Seat Booking (User A Thread -> Striped Seat Lock -> Seat State -> User B Thread).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Balance polymorphism against indirection, and striped locks against coarse synchronization. In production services, the LLD domain core (Entities, FSMs, Strategies) has zero framework or database imports—it depends only on narrow port interfaces (`Clock`, `SeatStore`.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Practice full end-to-end LLD implementations across caching, scheduling, and concurrency.

learningJourney.title: Why boolean flags and check-then-act races break services

explanation.foundation: Poor LLD produces god classes, brittle `if-else` trees, and concurrency bugs at 100k+ lines of code.
explanation.core: Two failure modes recur constantly: **boolean flag explosion** (`isActive`, `isPaused`, `isDeleted` allowing illegal states) and **check-then-act race conditions** where two threads both see `spot.isFree() == true` and issue duplicate tickets.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Low-Level System Design: LRU Cache, Elevator & Ticket Booking without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When a single bottleneck threatens end-to-end availability, elevator & Ticket Booking, great LLD isolates volatile business rules behind narrow interfaces and explicit state transitions so adding a new pricing rule, eviction policy, or booking workflow never breaks existing code.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.
